d: A chest monster with a pair of film reels on its lid. It is really a projector: place it with its mouth toward a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off. Right-click to open the controls. Its trick: right-click it with a chiseled block and it takes on the look and the name of that block (the chiseled block is not used up). To undo it, pick it up and put it back down. Sneak and right-click with a chiseled block to place it next to the mimic instead.

A chest monster with a telescoping antenna and tuning knobs on its lid. It is really a radio: it faces you when placed. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls. Its trick: right-click it with a chiseled block and it takes on the look and the name of that block (the chiseled block is not used up). To undo it, pick it up and put it back down. Sneak and right-click with a chiseled block to place it next to the mimic instead.

A streamlined 1950s radio in turquoise with a cream fascia in a chrome rim, chrome grille bars, a big round dial with a red needle and a stepped crest on top. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

An 80s boombox: a black case with two speakers, a cassette window, a glowing green tuner, piano keys, a carrying handle and a telescopic antenna. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A classic wooden cathedral radio with a cloth speaker grille, a brass dial and three black knobs. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A gothic arched radio in dark red wood and iron, with gold crosses and a glowing amber lattice. It plays everything a Smart TV does (YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups, hearing range) but has no screen: sound only. Right-click to open the controls.

A gramophone: a mahogany cabinet with a felt turntable, a black record with a red label, a brass tonearm, a hand crank and the big flared brass horn that amplifies the sound. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A hand-crank emergency radio: a black case with a carrying strap, a lit scale window with a red pointer, a round perforated speaker, a big selector knob with tuning, power-source and volume wheels, a telescoping antenna and a folding crank on its side. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls. You can also carry it: while it is anywhere in your hotbar it plays like the walkman, and other players within 6 blocks of you hear it. Right-click it in the air, or press U, for the controls. To set it down, sneak and right-click a block.

A 1950s jukebox: a cherry-red arched cabinet with chrome ribs, a rainbow of glowing neon bands round a window full of records, a selector panel with a coin slot and a chrome grille. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A 1960s space-age radio: a polished silver ball on a tulip pedestal with a turquoise band, a glowing amber tuning window, a louvred speaker grille and four swept-back whip antennas. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A steampunk radio: a walnut box with brass brackets, a pressure gauge, a glowing tuning window, a big flared brass horn and four glowing vacuum tubes. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.

A World War II army field radio: an olive-drab steel case with a canvas carrying strap, a big tuning dial, a perforated speaker, a red pilot lamp, a whip antenna and a handset hanging on its side. Sound only, otherwise it works like a Smart TV: YouTube and links, search, queue, linked groups and hearing range. Right-click to open the controls.
Wall-mounted TV. Right-click it, paste a YouTube link, and everyone nearby watches and hears it together.
A rounded 1950s TV with a chrome-rimmed screen on a wooden base. Sits on a table or the floor; the screen size is fixed.
An early flat TV with a silver frame and a desk stand. Widescreen. The screen size is fixed.
A big black 90s TV on a swivel base, with speaker grilles under the screen. The screen size is fixed.
Admin-only TV. Only admins can place, break or control it; everyone can watch.
A steampunk copper set with brass gears, pipes, levers and a pressure gauge.

3 blocks wide, 3 tall. An ivy-covered apothecary: shelf towers with stained-glass windows, potions, books, a mortar and pestle, a cow skull and brass scales, a horned crest with a glowing crystal vial, lavender, herb bundles, leaf banners and gnarled root legs with mushrooms. Needs room to place.
A brass telescope on a tripod, wrapped in glowing rune bands. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.
Frameless wall screen: just the picture, edge to edge. Great for big walls and cinemas.

A hulking skeletal film projector: a ribcage barrel with a glowing lens ringed by tusks, bone reels with skull hubs and a drive chain, clawed skeleton legs, a bone platform hung with banners with gold crosses, candles, a lantern in a hanging ribcage and skulls everywhere. 3 blocks wide, 3 deep and 3 tall, so it needs room. Place it looking at a wall and the picture comes out of the lens onto that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off. Glows softly.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A frame made entirely of bones: skulls on every corner, rib wings, a ribcage on the back and skeletal legs. Needs room to place.
A brass owl on a log whose glowing amber eyes cast the picture. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.
A screen on the ceiling, picture facing down, for watching lying down. Place it against the ceiling; the picture's top points back toward where you stood.

A glowing crystal ball held in gold claws on a carved stone pedestal. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.

3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A frame of amethyst and blue crystal: crystal clusters on the top, corners and sides, hanging gems, crossed crystal legs and a lattice back. Gives off a soft purple glow. Needs room to place.
Free-standing screen with a picture on both sides. Hang it from a ceiling or stand it in the middle of a room.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. An obsidian frame crowned with a dragon's head with glowing eyes and spread wings. Needs room to place.
A horned dragon skull with glowing ember eyes. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. Carved grey stone with gold knotwork, glowing rune plaques, a gold dwarf face under an arched crest and a gem emblem. Needs room to place.
3 blocks wide, 2 tall. Carved stone with gold trim and two burning braziers. Needs room to place.
The picture sits inside a living tree trunk with a leafy crown and roots.

A towering altar of a projector: a giant bloodshot eye with a glowing pupil in a riveted brass ring, held up by red tentacles on a claw-footed platform, with candelabras, tattered banners, chains with eye medallions and a crowd of small watching eyes. 3 blocks wide, 3 deep and 3 tall, so it needs room. Place it looking at a wall and the picture comes out of the pupil onto that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off. Glows softly.
A classic film projector. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.
A screen that lies flat on the floor, picture facing up. Great for dance floors: sink it one block down and cover it with glass. The picture's top points the way you faced when placing it.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A gilded mirror frame with a crest, a gem and lit candle sconces. Needs room to place.
A 90s TV on a wall bracket arm. Look at a wall and place it. The screen size is fixed.
A bright red 90s kids' TV with yellow knobs and a tiny antenna. The screen size is fixed.
A small white 2000s TV with a carry handle. Fits on a counter or shelf. The screen size is fixed.
An old wood-and-brass magic lantern that glows softly. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.
A sleek home theater projector. Place it looking at a wall and the picture appears on that wall. Picture distance and size are adjustable. Shows nothing while off.

3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A plank frame loaded with plunder: a skull in a tricorn over crossed cutlasses, gold chains and coins, tattered banners, a Jolly Roger, glowing lanterns, a ship's wheel, treasure chests and a little cannon. Needs room to place.
A 1980s portable TV with a carry handle and rabbit-ear antennas. Sits on a table or the floor; the screen size is fixed.

A big, solid black rear-projection TV from the 90s: a thin-framed dark screen above a speaker cabinet with a cloth panel, two side speakers, a control strip and vent slots, and a deep rounded back. 3 blocks wide, 3 tall, with a fixed screen size. Needs room to place: stand where the middle-bottom of the set should go.
A chunky old-school TV set. Stands on a table or the floor; the screen size is fixed.

3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A gothic console of stone and dark oak: pinnacled towers with armored knights carrying skull shields in their niches, a crowned golden skull crest over crossed swords, red swags and skull banners, candles, a screen in a gold-studded frame and a cabinet with fleur-de-lis doors. Plank back with iron straps, skull knockers and stained-glass windows. Needs room to place.
A mossy standing stone with the picture carved in, ringed by softly glowing runes.
A tall gold-framed standing mirror. The video plays in the glass.
A 2000s flat-front silver TV with a built-in DVD player. The screen size is fixed.

The big rear-projection TV in silver: a brushed-silver case with a dark screen, a charcoal cloth speaker panel, two side speakers, a control strip with a red standby light, vent slots and a deep rounded back. 3 blocks wide, 3 tall, with a fixed screen size. Needs room to place: stand where the middle-bottom of the set should go.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A copper and brass contraption with glowing vacuum tubes, a gramophone horn, a boiler, gears and gauges. Needs room to place.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A rusted iron frame wrapped in copper pipes, with glowing tubes, gauges, a gear crest, a lantern and piston feet. Needs room to place.
3 blocks wide, 3 tall. A stone archway whose opening shows the video, with glowing runes. Needs room to place.
A late-90s TV with a built-in tape player. The screen size is fixed.
A 1970s wooden TV cabinet on legs, with brass knobs and a speaker grille. Stands on the floor; the screen size is fixed.

A smartphone in a case printed like the back of a playing card. It plays like the walkman while it is anywhere in your hotbar, but it has a screen: hold it in your offhand (or in your hand) and you watch the video right on the phone, and only you see the picture. Other players hear it from its speaker within 6 blocks of you, getting quieter with distance. Press U to open the controls (an item in the offhand cannot be right-clicked). Sneak and right-click the top of a block to lay it down on the ground; it has no controls and does not play there, so pick it up again to listen.

A pocket cassette player with a pair of gothic headphones. It plays music from YouTube and other links while it is anywhere in your hotbar. You hear it as loud as you set it; other players only hear it quietly, within 2 blocks of you. Right-click it in the air, or press U, to open the controls. Sneak and right-click the top of a block to lay it down on the ground; it has no controls and does not play there, so pick it up again to listen.
